# Malawi

The wealth gradients this library holds for Malawi: first the values to give OG-Core, then the measurements behind them. New to the terms? See the [glossary](../glossary.md).

## What to use in OG-Core

| OG-Core input | Tilt | From |
|---|---|---|
| `fert_gradient` | **by age**, table below (fertility tilt −0.60 plus the [age offsets](../methods/fertility-by-age.md)) | DHS 2024 |
| `infmort_gradient` | **−0.04** | DHS 2024 |
| `mort_gradient` | **−0.28** (ages 15–60) | census 2008, own measurement |
| `imm_pctiles` | not covered by this library | — |

Every value is a **tilt** ([what that is](../glossary.md#tilt)). Convert it before passing it to OG-Core: `tilt / (100 × (1 − p))`, with p OG-Core's own rate at that age ([how](../methods/ogcore-units.md)).

**Fertility tilt by mother's age** (for `fert_gradient`; ages under 15 take the 15–19 value, 50 and over the 45–49 value):

| 15–19 | 20–24 | 25–29 | 30–34 | 35–39 | 40–44 | 45–49 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| −1.37 | −0.70 | −0.39 | −0.27 | −0.50 | −0.99 | −1.58 |

> **Note.** The 2008 census links only 99% of deaths to household assets: the tilt is usable, the death-rate levels are not.

## Where these numbers come from

### Household surveys (DHS)

Latest survey, from [`data/gradient_library_latest.csv`](../../data/gradient_library_latest.csv). Earlier surveys are in `gradient_library.csv`.

| Measure | Survey | Tilt | Poorest-to-richest ratio | Poorest fifth → richest fifth |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Births per woman (TFR) | 2024 | **−0.60** | 1.6 | 4.7 · 4.1 · 3.7 · 3.5 · 2.8 |
| Infant deaths per 1,000 births (IMR) | 2024 | **−0.04** | 1.0 | 35 · 32 · 40 · 35 · 32 |
| Under-5 deaths per 1,000 births (U5MR) | 2024 | **−0.24** | 1.2 | 53 · 49 · 54 · 48 · 42 |

### Adult mortality from censuses

Tilts of the death rate across household wealth, from [`data/adult_mortality_gradients.csv`](../../data/adult_mortality_gradients.csv) ([method](../methods/adult-mortality.md)). Men and women together where available; the by-sex rows are in the [full table](../tables/adult_mortality.md). A blank cell had too few deaths to publish.

| Census | Ages 15–60 | 15–29 | 30–44 | 45–59 | 60–74 | Wealth groups | Deaths |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1998 | **−0.02** | −0.32 | −0.06 | 0.12 |  | 4 | 6,380 |
| 2008 | **−0.28** | −0.71 | −0.50 | −0.10 |  | 4 | 5,243 |

Source: IPUMS International (Ruggles et al., doi:10.18128/D020.V7.7); original data: National Statistical Office, Malawi.

## Notes

- Two censuses (1998, 2008) make Malawi the worked example that the gradient steepens as income rises: the measured 45q15 tilt moved from −0.02 to −0.28 as income per head roughly doubled, within 0.07 of what the general gradient's income rule predicts.
